scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8142: Since the maintenance people fiddled with our Campus 2
access switch (switch4), HALF THE FLOOR is convinced the network is broken --
people on our two segments (the 10.5.0.x folks and the 10.6.0.x folks) say
they can't reach their gateway things any more. The maintenance have
OBVIOUSLY knocked one of our floors clean off that switch's uplink -- a whole
segment has fallen off the trunk, that is ALWAYS what happens after they
visit!! Please put the missing segment back on switch4's uplink and tell them
to stop touching things!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. switch4's trunk to sshswitch carries both
  VLAN 5 and VLAN 6, and both forward: VLAN 5 hosts (PC1, PC2, dc_pc5) reach
  10.5.0.254 and VLAN 6 hosts (PC3, PC4) reach 10.6.0.254, each with 0% loss. The
  correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of a
  trunk/VLAN-pruning fault on switch4 that is not occurring (cf.
  kath4-switch4-trunk-vlan5-down, where the VLAN 5 trunk subinterface IS down).

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- switch4's trunk dropping
VLAN 5 or VLAN 6 so hosts lose their uplink -- is NOT reproducible: both VLANs
forward over the trunk. PC1 (VLAN 5) reaches 10.5.0.254 with 0% loss and PC3
(VLAN 6) reaches 10.6.0.254 with 0% loss, confirming both VLANs traverse switch4
to sshswitch.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: switch4's trunk carries both VLANs and
the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the VLAN 5 and
VLAN 6 host->gateway paths, finds both working, checks that switch4's trunk
subinterfaces are up, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a pruned/dropped
VLAN -- blaming switch4's trunk to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The campus access switch (switch4) and its uplink are healthy; both affected VLANs (10.5.0.0/24 and 10.6.0.0/24) have intact L2 and L3 to their gateways. On switch4 the uplink uses VLAN subinterfaces eth0.5 and eth0.6, each bridged to the correct access ports (br_vlan5: eth0.5, eth1, eth2, eth3, eth6; br_vlan6: eth0.6, eth4, eth5). Both subinterfaces are UP. On the gateway side (sshswitch), the SVIs br_v5 (10.5.0.254/24) and br_v6 (10.6.0.254/24) are UP and include the trunk-facing subinterfaces eth0.5 and eth0.6.

Mechanism check: multiple hosts on each segment can ARP and ping their gateway. From VLAN 5: pc1, pc2, and dc_pc5 all successfully ping 10.5.0.254 and receive ARP replies from MAC be:d1:e2:a1:f9:d8. From VLAN 6: pc3 and pc4 successfully ping 10.6.0.254 and ARP the same gateway MAC. Topology-wide probes also show normal cross-VLAN reachability.

Localization: Uplink ms1_sw4 between switch4.eth0 and sshswitch.eth0 is operational and carrying both VLANs; gateways are on sshswitch br_v5/br_v6.

Root cause: No trunk/VLAN fault found; the reported outage was likely transient during maintenance or limited to specific endpoints.

Corrective fix: No network changes required. If users still report issues, have desktop support renew DHCP/flush ARP or verify NICs are connected to the correct access ports; the infrastructure path is confirmed good.

per_axis.rationale: Agent confirms the trunk carries both VLANs and hosts can reach their gateways but fails to explicitly state the required 0% packet-loss baseline.
